find-a-usable-chainpoint.text: Before reading, the terminal intersects accepted anchor publications with the provider’s retained views and history coverage. It selects the network, chainpoint and scheme, then acquires that exact view. Availability may change, so acquisition confirms the lease or refuses. No overlap means wait, switch provider or explicitly select another acceptable point, never mix answers.

session-contract.text: The state diagram starts with a selected chainpoint and either acquires a retained view or refuses. Active sessions support repeated reads, can expire or close, and can encounter rollback. The rollback branch explicitly has no decided outcome. This is separate from silently rebinding a session. Chainpoint means genesis or slot and block-header hash; the network is separate context.

storage-separation.text: The diagram connects a session to retained index roots, content references and immutable bytes. Stored bytes alone do not prove live membership. RocksDB snapshot handles do not survive restart; durable views need a chosen storage design, such as versioned nodes, persisted overlays or database checkpoints. A storage checkpoint is not a Cardano chainpoint.

history-coverage-before-costing.text: The roots and reconstruction workstream owns history coverage. Choose it before sizing the provider. Declare full-chain or filtered coverage, starting point, backfill, retention, all reference dependencies and refusals. Demonstrate deterministic replay to the authenticated root before cost commitments. Complete transaction CBOR is retained for each covered transaction.

decisions.text: Explicit chainpoint selection replaces mixing latest responses. Bounded views make availability commitments finite, and immutable content allows payloads to be shared across views.

open-questions.text: Resolve abandoned-branch sessions, leases, atomic view contents, discovery wire formats, history coverage and retry policy. The initial model must expose acquisition, reads, rollback, expiry and eviction.
